title: Tomato and Basil Bruschetta
summary: Thick slices of charred country bread rubbed with garlic and piled high with ripe red and yellow tomatoes and fresh basil.
equipment: grill pan, barbecue or oven grill (broiler)

ingredients.item: ripe red and yellow tomatoes, cored and cut into 1 cm dice
fine sea salt or table salt
thick slices of rustic country bread, about 2 cm

steps.title: Salt and drain
steps.text: Toss the diced tomatoes with the salt in a sieve set over a bowl and leave for 15 minutes. The salt draws out excess juice, concentrating the flavour and keeping the toast from going soggy. Tip away the juice.

steps.title: Dress the tomatoes
steps.text: Mix the drained tomatoes in the bowl with the basil, 2 tbsp olive oil and the pepper. Shredding the basil finely spreads its aroma through every spoonful without large, wilting leaves.

steps.title: Char the bread
steps.text: Heat the grill pan over high heat, or the oven grill (broiler) to high. Toast the bread for 1-2 minutes a side, until crisp and golden with dark char lines but still soft in the middle. A crisp surface with a tender centre gives the best contrast under the juicy topping.

steps.title: Garlic and oil
steps.text: While the toasts are hot, rub one side of each with the cut garlic, then brush with the remaining olive oil. The rough, hot surface acts like a grater, so the garlic melts into the bread.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Spoon the tomato mixture over the toasts with a slotted spoon, piling it high, and serve within 10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon leaves behind any liquid that collects in the bowl.

tips: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find; this dish depends on them, so in winter choose small, sweet varieties.
A common mistake is topping the toasts too early; assemble just before serving so the bread stays crisp.
Rub the garlic lightly at first and add more to taste, as raw garlic is strong.
A squeeze of lemon juice can brighten tomatoes that lack acidity.
storage: The topping can be made up to 2 hours ahead and kept at room temperature. Leftover topping keeps covered in the fridge for 1 day; let it come back to room temperature before using, and toast fresh bread. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
